title: American Samoa Historical Climate Data
html:
A partner project of the Hawai‘i Climate Data Portal

Historical Climate Data

Raw Climate Data

UH-ASPA stations have been in the field since 2015. Climate station data prior to August 2022 was recorded at 15 minute intervals and switched to 5 minute intervals at all climate stations. Stream gauge data is recorded at 15 minute intervals.

Cleaned Data

Due to various reasons, our weather stations have experienced gaps in their records, ranging from months to years. To manage this, a predictive model was created using XGBoost, a type of machine learning that utilizes gradient boosting methods to develop regression relationships between variables. Both our weather station data and other local stations were used in the data collection process to help train the model. So far, this has been used for our shorter gaps and stable meteorological variables.  The following data is cleaned and gap-filled from the above raw climate data.
  • Aasu
    • Relative Humidity  ↗ (opens in a new tab)

  • Vaipito

Daily Historical Data

Daily sum rainfall data in inches from climate stations in American Samoa. These data are collected from multiple agencies including the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), the University of Hawaii (UH), the Western Regional Climate Center (WRCC), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), and over a time period of 1958 to 2024. For some stations, sum daily rainfall has been calculated from sub-daily (15-minute or hourly) intervals.
Click the station name to access data.

The American Samoa Climate Data Portal is under development. If you would like to contribute any feedback or have questions, please fill out this google form: https://forms.gle/Puh1YKGYRa5RD5Gb9 ↗ (opens in a new tab) or email Chris Shuler (cshuler@hawaii.edu).
